ideas.description: Instrument and tip decision, with no recipe change. In untimed side scripts, run the unchanged E090 code (48b13a7) and the unchanged E095 code (0503e38) through the benchmark's own trial code on seeds 3-26: 24 seeds each, one fresh process per config so the cuDNN picks are resampled. Do not edit benchmark/. Log per-seed accuracy, per-seed final-weight checksums, and the cuDNN conv kernel names per (layer, shape) from the profiler in build and the first steps; this is the free by-product for H4.5.1. For the scored row, rerun E090 unchanged; a non-bit-identical result adds a third distinct tip sample. Store both 24-seed per-seed vectors as the paired baselines for every later off-seed A/B on seeds 3-26.
ideas.expected: Scored row: ~4.46 s (±0.5%), accuracy 0.751-0.754. Off-seed: per-seed sd 0.22-0.38 pp, so the 24-seed SE is ~0.05-0.08 pp. E090 mean 0.7518-0.7530 and E095 mean 0.7535-0.7548, a gap of +0.1 to +0.2 pp. If E090 is >=0.7535, it counts as robustly banked and the pressure to add accuracy drops. If E095-E090 is <0.05 pp, the 28 px substitution was nearly free and further 32->28 substitution is reopened. No time change.

ideas.description: Math-neutral FLOP-free time lever. Base: E090 code. At the very start of build, before any conv runs, set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark_limit = 0 so that cuDNN v8 tries every available algorithm for each static train shape (16/24 px at bs 1536, 28/32 px at bs 1024, both whitening-bias-grad variants) and for the eval path, instead of the default 10. Change nothing else. Log the build time, which must stay <600 s, the per-phase epoch times, and the conv kernel names per (layer, shape), and diff the kernel names against the E090 defaults logged by the H4.2.7 run. Score twice and compare distinct samples against the E090 family.
ideas.expected: At least one 24/28/32 px conv shape picks a different kernel. Mean time -0.3 to -1.5% (about 4.40-4.45 s), mostly in the energy-bound 28/32 px phases. Build +10 to +60 s. Accuracy is math-equivalent within noise: distinct pool within 0.1 pp of the E090 family (~0.752-0.754). If the kernel names are identical to the defaults, or the time change is <0.3%, close the lever. If it is banked, it stacks on any later tip and also transfers to the PCIe judge, since it is per-kernel efficiency.

ideas.description: Path-length test, run directly on the tip so a positive result is immediately bankable. Deviation from the H10.2.1 text: it uses the E090 base instead of E086, so it reuses the seeds 3-26 E090 baseline from the H4.2.7 run and needs no new control. Base: E090 code. In the 32 px phase only (the final 2.75 epochs at bs 1024, floor-hold included), multiply the conv-filter Muon lr schedule by 1.25 (0.24 -> 0.30 at the same schedule position). The head keeps its 0.5x multiplier and scales along. The 16/24/28 px phases are unchanged. Implement it as a phase-keyed host-side factor written into the existing 0-d lr tensor, so nothing recompiles. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26, paired against the E090 baseline, plus two distinct scored samples.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, ~4.46 s). Path-length prediction: off-seed +0.05 to +0.12 pp (E090 gave back ~0.15-0.25 pp of 32 px exposure against E095, and more movement per 32 px step should recover part of it). A pass (off-seed >= +0.08 pp and a distinct scored mean >=0.7535) makes it the robust tip at ~4.46 s. If the gain is <= +0.03 pp, update count rather than movement is the mechanism, and only per-phase batch size (H2.11) remains. If the loss is >=0.1 pp, the late Muon lr is already at or above its optimum.

ideas.description: Resolution-statistics adaptation test (the 70% arm). Base: E090 code. Move the whitening-bias detach point from ~41% of samples (inside the 24 px phase) to ~70% of samples (inside the 32 px phase, after both the 28 and 32 px switches). Keep the bias LR schedule otherwise unchanged. Warm up the whiten_bias_grad=True graph variants for the 24 px bs-1536, 28 px bs-1024 and 32 px bs-1024 shapes in build on synthetic data. Change nothing else. Log the whitening-bias vector norm and its relative change across each resolution switch. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26, paired against the E090 baseline, plus two distinct scored samples.
ideas.expected: Time +0.3 to +0.8% (~4.48-4.50 s; the stem dgrad comes back for ~29% more of the samples). Adaptation prediction: off-seed +0.05 to +0.15 pp, with the bias changing by >=10% of its norm after the 28 and 32 px switches. A gain of >=0.1 pp beats the 0.065 pp per 1% bar and, with two feasible scored samples, makes it the tip. If the change is within ±0.05 pp and the bias barely moves after the switches, the freeze point is closed and E093's loss was early-phase fragility.

ideas.description: Discriminating test for end-of-run averaging, matching the H6.5.4 spec on the current tip. Base: E090 code. Replace the 8-step final EMA with E081's 20-step window (lerp 0.3 every 4 steps from 20 steps before the end, initialized from the net at the window start). Also lerp every BN running_mean/running_var buffer with the same weights, in the same foreach_lerp, instead of copying the buffers from the final net. EMA buffer copies are allocated in build and reset in prepare. The lookahead stop and floor-hold are unchanged, and nothing recompiles. Decide on off-seed seeds 3-26, paired against the E090 baseline. Add one scored run, and a second only if off-seed is >= +0.05 pp.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). BN-mismatch explanation: off-seed >= E090 +0.05 pp (against E081's -0.09 with copied buffers). Iterate-LR explanation: off-seed <= E090 -0.05 pp. If the BN explanation wins by >=0.08 pp, a follow-up adds BN-buffer averaging to the 8-step window as a free gain. If the iterate-LR explanation wins, end-of-run averaging and H6 close.

ideas.description: Explore depth cuts, untimed first. In a side script on E090 code, build two variants with recompile and warm-up: (a) group-1 conv3 removed and (b) group-3 conv3 removed. Muon stacks are re-batched for the changed filter counts. Measure per-step time with CUDA events and NVML energy over 20 steps each at 32 px bs 1024, 28 px bs 1024, 24 px bs 1536 and 16 px bs 1536, then project total run time over the E090 schedule. For the scored row, rerun E090 unchanged (another distinct tip sample). Score a depth variant later only if its projection shows >=6%.
ideas.expected: Projection: group-3 conv3 removal saves ~5-8% of run time (576-ch 3x3 GEMMs plus ~23 elementwise kernels, small maps). Group-1 conv3 removal saves ~4-7% (large 31x31 maps, elementwise-heavy). If either is >=6%, queue a scored arm that spends half the saving on extra 32 px samples (net ~-3%). If both are <6%, depth cuts close without a scored run. Scored row ~4.46 s, 0.751-0.754.

drop.reason: Its comparator, E083's -0.29 pp, was measured on E070-era code against a different tip baseline, and it uses seeds 3-10 (SE ~0.1-0.13 pp), so it cannot cleanly separate the two H6.5 mechanisms. Superseded by the new H6.5.4 idea, which follows the hypothesis spec (20-step EMA with BN buffers lerped) on E090 with the seeds 3-26 paired baseline.

structured_output.summary:
The tip, E090, runs at about 4.46 s but is feasible by luck: its distinct-sample mean is about 0.7524, below the 0.753 gate. The only robustly feasible config is E095 at about 4.70 s. Every way of shrinking the 32 px phase costs about 0.05-0.065 pp per 1% of time saved, so further gains must come from math-neutral speedups or from accuracy added at zero time.

**New ideas (6), by priority:**
- **Priority 5, H4.2.7:** run E090 and E095 on seeds 3-26 (untimed). This is the calibration step: it decides whether E090 is robust and provides the paired baseline for every later off-seed test. It also logs cuDNN kernel names for free (H4.5.1).
- **Priority 5, H2.14.5:** set `cudnn.benchmark_limit=0` in the untimed build. It is the last untested math-neutral time lever. Expected about -0.3% to -1.5% time.
- **Priority 4, H10.2.1:** raise the Muon lr by 1.25x in the 32 px phase only. I moved this onto E090 instead of E086 so it reuses the seeds 3-26 baseline and is bankable right away. If Muon's gain comes from total filter movement rather than step count, this recovers accuracy at zero time.
- **Priority 3, H11.1.1:** move the whitening-bias freeze from about 41% to about 70% of samples, testing whether the net needs to adapt after each resolution switch. Expected cost +0.3% to +0.8% time.
- **Priority 3, H6.5.4:** a 20-step final EMA that also averages the BN buffers. This decides between the two end-of-run averaging explanations; if neither shows an effect, H6 closes.
- **Priority 2, H2.18.1:** an untimed profile of removing one conv layer, which only gets a scored run if the projected saving is at least 6%.

**Kept in the queue:**
- **I104** (H10.1.1 / H11.2.1): one run tests both rival hypotheses about whether added low-res steps help.
- **I105** (H7.1.3): global Muon lr; it ranks below the 32 px-only test.

**Dropped:** I108. Its comparison baseline (E083) was measured on older code with only seeds 3-10, so it can't cleanly separate the two averaging explanations. The new H6.5.4 idea replaces it.

**Deferred:** H2.11.5 (bs 768 at 28/32 px). Its likely exchange rate only matches the trim rate, so it cannot pay for a net time cut. H2.4.3 (the projection to the 300 W PCIe judge) is only a tie-breaker.

The queue now has 8 queued ideas plus I102 running.
